findings.evidence: The raised ceiling also survives this chapter’s binding per-rank test: per-rank weights are 39.24375 ÷ 8 = 4.906 GB, leaving 80 − 4.906 − 8 = 67.09 GB of KV budget per rank, which holds 67.09 ÷ 3.11296 = 21.55 → floor 21 sequences — the same integer the aggregate division gives, so the ceiling is not an aggregate artifact.
findings.issue: The per-rank arithmetic silently changes the reserve basis. The aggregate calculation subtracts a fixed 64 GB host reserve (640 − 39.24375 − 64 = 536.75625 GB). The per-rank calculation subtracts 8 GB per rank, which is the 64 GB host reserve divided by 8. That is internally consistent, but the prose calls 8 GB “the full runtime-reserve share” without repeating that it is a host-level reserve divided across ranks. Because the preceding sentence says “per-rank weights are 39.24375 ÷ 8 = 4.906 GB, leaving 80 − 4.906 − 8 = 67.09 GB,” a reader can easily read the 8 GB as a per-rank measured reserve rather than as 64/8. The quantity has two possible meanings and the text does not disambiguate at the point of use.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite the per-rank sentence to say “the 64 GB host reserve divided by 8 ranks = 8 GB per rank” and label it as the same planning reserve, not a measured per-rank allocation. Keep the aggregate and per-rank reserve definitions adjacent so the 8 GB cannot be mistaken for an independent per-rank constant.

findings.evidence: Unit basis (locked): the H100's quoted 80 GB is treated as decimal 80×10^9 B throughout, so the canonical 8×H100 pool reads 640 GB. The vendor-binary reading is 81,559 MiB ≈ 85.5×10^9 B per part ... On the vendor-binary basis the aggregate test flips to passing (164.1 < 171.0 GB), but the per-rank test still fails (70 + 12.05 (per-rank FP16 KV, 24.1 ÷ 2) + ~32 GB reserve (the same ~64 GB host reserve divided across the 2 ranks, 64 ÷ 2) = 114.05 GB > 85.5 GB)
findings.issue: The vendor-binary per-rank arithmetic is wrong: 70 + 12.05 + 32 = 114.05 GB, which the text compares against 85.5 GB — but the components are in inconsistent units. On the vendor-binary basis the per-rank weight footprint is 140 GB ÷ 2 = 70 GB (decimal basis) while the per-part capacity is 85.5×10^9 B (also decimal), so that part is consistent; the error is that the per-rank KV of 24.1 ÷ 2 = 12.05 GB is the 9.2K input-only KV divided by 2 ranks, but the per-rank reserve is taken as 64 ÷ 2 = 32 GB, i.e. the entire 8-GPU host's reserve split across only 2 ranks. That assumption is stated, but it is then inconsistent with the 3-GPU conclusion it supports: if the reserve is a host-level pool that scales with host width, the 2-rank case should divide by 8 (the canonical host width) or the 64 GB figure should be scaled; the text picks whichever reading reproduces 'fails' in one place and 'passes' elsewhere. Worse, the decimal-basis per-rank test the chapter actually relies on (17.5 + 54.48 + 8 = 79.98 GB of 80 GB, p. 91) uses 8 GB = 64 ÷ 8, i.e. the reserve is per-GPU-share on a 8-GPU host — so a 2-GPU host would carry 8 GB per rank, not 32 GB, under the same rule. Using the same rule (64 ÷ 8 = 8 GB per rank) on the vendor-binary basis gives 70 + 12.05 + 8 = 90.05 GB > 85.5 GB — still fails, but by a different margin than the printed 114.05 GB, and the printed figure overstates the reserve threefold relative to the book's own rule.
findings.fix_instruction: State one reserve rule explicitly (e.g. 'the ~64 GB runtime/workspace reserve is a host-level planning pool that scales with host width; per-rank reserve = 64 ÷ (GPUs per host)') and apply it consistently: 8 GB per rank on the canonical 8-GPU host, and on the 2-rank vendor-binary alternative either state the alternative reserve assumption explicitly and its justification, or use the same per-rank rule and recompute the total (90.05 GB > 85.5 GB) rather than the printed 114.05 GB.

findings.evidence: The full-attention component of Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B illustrates the transfer from a configuration to a memory estimate. Its language configuration has 16 full-attention layers, four KV-heads per layer, and a head dimension of 256 ... With BF16 KV storage, the raw component is: 2 × 16 × 4 × 256 × 2 = 65,536 bytes per cached token. At 262,144 cached tokens, this component occupies 16 GiB (17,179,869,184 B ≈ 17.18 GB on the chapter's decimal GB basis, §7.1).
findings.issue: Arithmetic check: 262,144 × 65,536 = 17,179,869,184 B = 16 GiB exactly ✓, and 17,179,869,184 / 10^9 = 17.18 GB ✓ — this row is correct. The defect is a consistency one across the two usages of the same configuration: the same Qwen3.8-27B is described in Ch. 3 (p. 73) as having '16 full-attention layers' with '48 Gated DeltaNet layers', and Ch. 7 here confirms 16 full-attention layers, but Ch. 3 §3.6.1's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next paragraph describes a different sibling checkpoint (125B/6B) with 'Gated DeltaNet (GDN) on three of every four layers plus Qwen Sparse Attention (QSA) on the fourth' — i.e. a 3:1 GDN:QSA ratio, whereas the 27B checkpoint is 48:16 = 3:1 as well, which is consistent. The actual inconsistency is that Ch. 3 states 'Chapter 7 works a configuration-backed version of exactly this two-term budget — Qwen3.8-27B's 16 full-attention layers priced separately from its 48 Gated DeltaNet layers' while Ch. 7 §7.3.2 never states the 48 Gated DeltaNet layer count or prices the recurrent-state term M_recurrent; the formula 'M_history(L) = L × 65,536 bytes + M_recurrent' is given with M_recurrent as an undefined symbol, so the 'two-term budget' Ch. 3 advertises is not actually completed in Ch. 7.
findings.fix_instruction: In §7.3.2, state the second term explicitly: name the 48 Gated DeltaNet (plus convolution) language layers, state that their recurrent/convolution state is fixed-shape and independent of L, give its size or state clearly that it is unmeasured and excluded, and then the M_history expression is a completed two-term budget rather than a formula with an undefined symbol.

findings.chapter: Ch. 7 — Memory Is the First Constraint (opening, Architect's Question)
findings.evidence: Ch. 7's opening: "We will build the arithmetic for the KV cache from first principles, reconcile it with the canonical ~1.31 MB/token figure from Chapter 1" — but the same page later states "the canonical scenario's KV constant is the FP16 2.62 MB/token figure, not the 8-bit ~1.31 MB/token number" and calls 1.31 "Chapter 1's reference figure". Ch. 1 (PDF p. 32) agrees: "The canonical scenario's KV constant is the FP16 figure, ~2.62 MB/token". Ch. 7 §7.4 itself warns: "Do not assume the 1.3 MB/token figure applies at FP16 — it does not".
findings.issue: The word "canonical" is misapplied to the 8-bit ~1.31 MB/token figure in the chapter's opening question. In this book's taxonomy [canonical scenario] pins the FP16 2.62 MB/token constant; the sentence commits the exact 8-bit/FP16 conflation the chapter later lists as a measurement mistake.
findings.fix_instruction: Change "the canonical ~1.31 MB/token figure from Chapter 1" to "the ~1.31 MB/token 8-bit reference figure from Chapter 1" in the Ch. 7 opening; sweep the book for any other use of "canonical" attached to the 1.31 MB/token value.

findings.chapter: Ch. 7 — Memory Is the First Constraint (§7.1.1 and §7.2.1)
findings.evidence: Two bare Axis-2-only tags: §7.1.1 ends "...it changes what must be inventoried before that budget's arithmetic is reused for a different generation mechanism. [DERIVED]"; §7.2.1 ends "Static prompt embeddings can remain reusable, but that is not the growing autoregressive cache. [DERIVED]". The Preface (PDF p. 20) requires: "A label pair always takes one item from each of the first two axes, e.g. [1P][DERIVED] or [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]".
findings.issue: Malformed evidence labels: [DERIVED] appears without its mandatory Axis-1 provenance partner, violating the book's own label-pair rule; every other inline tag in the visible text is a pair.
findings.fix_instruction: Either pair each tag with an Axis-1 value (e.g. [canonical scenario][DERIVED] for statements derived from the canonical mechanism, or [1P][DERIVED] where a named first-party source grounds it) or delete the tags, since both sentences are qualitative mechanism statements rather than load-bearing quantities.

findings.chapter: Ch. 7 — Memory Is the First Constraint (Table 7-1)
findings.evidence: Table 7-1 row: "inference residency (weights + KV, 128K) | ≈ 475 GB | 140 + 335.5 GB" — but 140 + 335.5 = 475.5, and the same table's 128K fit note below prints "475.5 GB < 640 GB". Sibling rows round correctly ("≈ 165 GB" from 164.9; "≈ 224 GB" from 223.9).
findings.issue: Rounding inconsistency inside one table: the 128K residency value column truncates 475.5 GB to "≈ 475 GB" while the derivation column and the fit note both carry 475.5 GB, unlike every other row which rounds its own sum correctly.
findings.fix_instruction: Print the value as "≈ 475.5 GB" (or 476 GB) in the residency row so the value column, derivation column and fit note agree.

findings.chapter: Chapter 7 — Memory Is the First Constraint
findings.evidence: PDF p.21: 'Arithmetic belongs on the epistemic-status axis, not the provenance axis: a worked example computed from a model card is [1P][DERIVED], never [2°].' PDF p.22: 'The deployment unit those constants are priced into — an 8×H100 host — is a scenario choice, not a vendor fact: [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION], as Table 4-2 records it.' PDF p.160: '3×H100 total VRAM / 3 ×80 GB = 240 GB / 3 × the vendor’s 80 GB per-part constant [1P] / [FACT] (NVIDIA H100 80 GB specification); like the 2× and 8× rows and the 640 GB pool in Table 7-2, the capacity is a [1P][FACT] vendor constant'
findings.issue: Derived aggregate host-memory capacities are labeled as first-party facts. The 2×/3×/8× H100 totals and the 640 GB pool are arithmetic over a vendor per-part constant plus a scenario-defined host composition, not vendor-stated facts; this contradicts the book's own evidence rules.
findings.fix_instruction: Relabel aggregate capacity rows such as 2×H100, 3×H100, 8×H100, and the 640 GB pool as [1P][DERIVED] from the [1P][FACT] per-GPU VRAM constant, with the host composition tied to [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] where it is used. Sweep the same aggregate-capacity label pattern in Table 7-2 and any later recurrence.
